The Proposition

Part One

The Proposition

What the Board is asked to resolve, and the three decisions the rest of this document exists to inform.

The Proposition
Not a decisionThe Board of Academic Standards has no appointed members and no External Examiner has been appointed. Both are appointments rather than engineering tasks, and until they are made the College cannot confer.
StatusBOARD DECISION REQUIRED

Three resolutions

This plan asks for three decisions and no others. Everything else in it is either a fact about the College, which is marked as one, or a consequence of arithmetic the Board can check.

One · The revenue-allocation framework

That gross collected revenue be governed as 25% payroll, 5% technology, 10% operating, 10% marketing, 25% reserve, 25% strategic. The two retained lines are designated institutional capital; the Strategic and Founders’ Allocation is not automatically withdrawable income, and no distribution from it is modelled anywhere in this plan.

Two · The tariff that follows from it

That the tariff be set at the cheapest point satisfying that framework — a Tutored pathway at $27,900. The price is the output of the framework rather than a management preference, and it moves if the framework moves.

Three · The two channels the portfolio lacks

That the College open Corporate and Institutional agreements at its own published partner bands. A purely retail College could not bring acquisition below 22% of revenue against a 10% target, because a cost incurred one learner at a time never amortises.

Part Two

The Institution

What the College is, what it sells, and the discipline that makes both statements checkable.

The Institution
What is not claimedNo accreditation, no ranking, no institutional partnership, no external endorsement. No completed cohort. No External Examiner has confirmed the standard.
The pathway1,200 academic hours · 6 levels · 120 credits · A1 to C2

Identity

WorldWide English College teaches a 1,200-hour qualification pathway in six levels from A1 to C2, examined against rubrics published before the work, second-marked, moderated, and entered in a registry a stranger can check without an account.

The credential is identical whichever route a candidate takes to it — same examination, same rubric, same second marking, same moderation, same registry entry, same public verification. The routes differ in price by a factor of thirty-eight because what they differ in is human attention, which is the only thing here that actually costs money.

What it does hold

A complete six-level curriculum; an examination architecture with second marking and moderation; a published fee decomposition accounting for every cent of a fee; a conferral and verification chain; and fourteen typeset volumes of its own curriculum and assessment work, free to anyone, enrolled or not.

The discipline

Every figure in this publication is computed by one engine from four files. None is typed into a page, and the reconciliation is run as a test on every build rather than asserted as a claim.

12
The Institution

The academic architecture

Six gates, and what passes each

The College’s own plate, drawn in engraved line.

What a gate is

Each level ends at an examination set against a rubric published before the work begins, marked by a named person, marked a second time independently, and moderated across the cohort. Nothing passes on attendance, and nothing passes on a tutor’s recommendation alone.

A candidate who does not pass sits again; one re-sit is included and there is no re-sit fee on either route. A candidate who passes is entered in the registry the same day, and the entry can be checked by anyone, without an account, for as long as the College exists.

Why six, and why this size

A level is 200 academic hours because that is roughly what the Common European Framework takes to move an adult one band, and because 4 instalments across 4 months is a commitment a working adult can actually make.

Each level confers its own award. A learner who stops after two holds two qualifications rather than a fraction of one, which is the difference between a pathway and a course somebody abandoned.

The credential is identical on every route. What a route changes is how much of a named instructor’s attention the candidate receives on the way to it — and that, not the certificate, is what the tariff is pricing.

Rejecting well is most of the job

Thirty candidate sources were pulled and eight shipped. What did not survive is recorded beside what did, because an undocumented rejection gets re-proposed six months later by somebody who does not know it was already considered.

Four markets carry no direct observation at all. They are modelled from the segments that do, and marked as modelled on every page they appear. The plan does not convert an absence of evidence into a number and hope nobody checks.

19
The Market

No provider found sells a six-level, 1,200-hour credentialed pathway as one purchase. WEC-LC’s product does not have a market price, because the product is not on the market.

That is why this plan prices per level and per hour of a named instructor’s attention rather than comparing pathway totals. A pathway total has no comparable. An hour of a qualified teacher’s attention has one everywhere.

Commercial Architecture

The comparison that survives

Per hour of individual attention

The only like-for-like unit available, and each tier against the comparable it actually has.

A pathway total has no comparable. An hour of a qualified teacher’s attention has one everywhere — and a group module and a one-to-one programme have different ones.

23
Commercial Architecture
Directed, stated plainlyAt $404 an hour of attention and $119 a contact hour, Directed is dearer than the British Council on both measures. It is the one tier in the tariff that cannot be defended on price.

What the figure shows

Independent and Tutored sit below the British Council’s published Saudi tariff per hour of individual instructor attention, and confer an award the module does not. All three Executive tiers sit inside the executive coaching band of $200 to $600, which is the right comparable for one-to-one provision and the wrong one to have ignored.

And the tier that does not

Directed is dearer than the benchmark on both measures. An earlier draft of this plan claimed the College was cheaper at every tier; that was true at a lower tariff, was never re-checked when the price rose, and is false. It survived a table of six numbers and did not survive being drawn.

Directed’s defence is therefore not its hourly rate. It is that the fee carries the examination, second marking, moderation, the registry entry and the conferral, none of which a language module includes. Management states that rather than a price advantage it does not have.

Why the channels exist

What one negotiation buys

Acquisition paid per learner never amortises; paid per agreement it divides by the seats it carries.

Swept across a twelvefold price range and a sixteenfold range of scale, a purely retail College could not bring acquisition below 22 per cent of revenue against a 10% target. The bands are the College’s own published policy, not invented ones. MODELLED

The institutional channels removed the trade an earlier draft was built around: the proposal now earns more on every dimension than the adopted flat tariff.

What changed, and why the comparison did

An earlier draft reported a genuine trade: the proposed portfolio reached more learners than the adopted flat tariff and gave up surplus to do it. The plan said so, and a test in the build forbade it from claiming otherwise.

Adding the institutional channels removed the trade. A sponsored cohort reaches people a retail price cannot and pays acquisition once for all of them, so the proposal now earns more revenue, more surplus, more learners and more awards at the same time.

The test was inverted rather than deleted. It checks the shape of the comparison instead of its direction, because a guard that forbids a true claim is as bad as one that permits a false one.

Part Five

The Financial
Architecture

Where every dollar of collected revenue is governed, and what each line is forbidden from becoming.

Financial Architecture

Definitions

What each line is, and is not

Payroll

All employed people: academic delivery, examinations, registry, admissions, student support, platform engineering, academic standards, finance and compliance, and institutional leadership, inclusive of on-costs.

25%

LMS and Technology

The learning platform, hosting, authentication, storage, media, security and the tooling the College runs on. Salaries of the people who build it sit in Payroll.

5%

Operating Expenses

Legal, accounting, insurance, audit, professional services, the London registered office, examinations administration, and institutional administration.

10%

Marketing and Student Acquisition

Media, content, campaigns, partnership development and the admissions conversation — the cost of being found and understood. Salaries of the people who do it sit in Payroll.

10%

Institutional Reserve

Restricted or designated institutional capital retained to strengthen liquidity, fund major institutional initiatives, absorb exceptional shocks, support future expansion, and maintain long-term financial resilience.

Not distributable. Not a surplus line. Not available to fund ordinary operating shortfalls without a recorded Board resolution.

25%

Strategic and Founders' Allocation

A discretionary institutional allocation available for founder remuneration, strategic investment, expansion, intellectual property development, new campuses and markets, acquisitions, exceptional executive compensation, and other Board-authorised strategic purposes.

NOT automatically withdrawable founder income, and the plan never presents it as profit. Any distribution from it is a separate Board decision on a separate occasion.

25%

The Core Plan is management’s recommended execution case, not the midpoint of the other two.

What a scenario has to change to be one

A scenario set whose only variable is “more students” tests nothing. Each of these changes something the College would actually have to do differently: what it costs to be found, how many learners continue from one level to the next, and how far the College can reach at all.

The Conservative case does not reach cumulative surplus inside the decade. That is stated rather than smoothed, because it is the plan’s real exposure — the Core case requires continuation and reach to hold broadly as modelled, and reach is the one quantity here that was never researched.

Part Six

The Decade

Five phases, twenty risks each with a warning somebody can observe, and who decides what.

The Decade

The ten-year roadmap

Five phases, and what has to be true at the end of each

IFoundationYears 1–2

Open the Gulf and West Africa. Appoint the academic offices. Publish the first examination papers and confer the first awards. Prove the qualification end to end before spending to be known.

354 under instruction · $1.4M net tuition

IIValidationYears 3–4

Europe opens. Break-even is cleared and the reserve begins. Continuation, not acquisition, becomes the measure that matters. The External Examiner confirms the standard against published rubrics.

1,150 under instruction · $4.8M net tuition

IIIScaleYears 5–7

Asia opens. Sponsored cohorts become a material and deliberate share of enrolment — one negotiation carrying a cohort at a published band rather than learners acquired one at a time. The establishment is fully staffed and the institution stops depending on any one person.

3,463 under instruction · $14.8M net tuition

IVMaturityYears 8–9

Reserve builds toward its target in months of operating cost. Accreditation is pursued with a completed cohort and an examiner’s confirmation behind it, not before.

3,851 under instruction · $17.0M net tuition

VStandingYears 10

The institution is self-funding, externally examined, internationally enrolled, and holds a register of awards a stranger can check without an account.

3,851 under instruction · $17.0M net tuition

A planning instrument,
and not a record of trading.

Every financial figure in this publication is a projection computed from stated assumptions. Where the College holds something it is marked VERIFIED; where this plan asserts something, MODELLED; where nobody has yet decided, BOARD DECISION REQUIRED.

The College claims no accreditation, ranking, partnership or endorsement it does not hold, and names no person in an office they have not accepted.
